reason: The quoted numbers are copied correctly, but the key one misleads. Q's 'equal-exposure' gain of -6.4% (leak5 OOF 1.4278 vs 1.5254 um) is a pooled figure, and 6bba supplies 106k of its 126k pairs. Splitting the leak5 folds by embryo (out_full_Q/report.json, per_embryo, pair-weighted) gives two different pictures. On 44b6, Q is +5.1% WORSE than the public head even in-embryo (1.3624 vs 1.2963 um; P is +7.8% worse). On 6bba, Q is only -3.3% better (1.5150 vs 1.5668). The metric matches at 7 um and relinks on relative positions, so a uniform per-video offset barely matters. With the bias removed (sqrt(mean^2 - |bias|^2)), Q vs public in-embryo is +3.0% on 44b6 and -5.0% on 6bba. Out-of-embryo, Q's 6bba advantage disappears: 1.336 in-embryo becomes 1.424 out-of-embryo, +1.3% vs public in-embryo. That is the transfer signal: the extra gain is embryo-specific. On 6bba, where the loss lives, the public head itself beats no head by only -4.1% bias-removed (-8.9% raw, mostly z-offset correction). Blend value: by the convexity bound, blend^2 <= 0.5(a^2+b^2) - 0.25 E|s_pub - s_Q|^2. With both heads regressing the same residual (shift cosine ~0.7, a guess), the averaging bonus is about -1.3% distance, and it only offsets Q's own +0..+4% deficit. Best estimate on an unseen embryo: blend vs public = -1.3% +- 1.5% mean distance. Slope: x138's +0.007 for the public head's -9.5%, minus a possible ~+0.0027 node-multiplier share (the head cut final nodes by -2.9%, DIFF.md section 4). On our base the same head gave +0.002. So 0.0005-0.001 LB per 1%, and the blend is worth about +0.001 (range -0.001 to +0.003). That is below the +0.002 bar and a third of the 0.003 LB noise, so one probe cannot confirm it, and the rule 'adopt if public >= #34' is close to a coin flip. The idea's own pre-registered gate (b) (blend <= 0.95 x public on EACH embryo) also fails almost surely on 44b6. Q is +5.1% worse there in-embryo, so passing needs the two heads' shifts to be nearly uncorrelated (cosine <= ~0.3). Gate (a) on 6bba->44b6 is roughly a tie at best. P(gate pass) is about 0.1-0.15, not 0.35. The idea does have one fair point: the comparator asymmetry is real, because the public head saw about 10 overlapping 44b6 crops and 10 6bba videos. But no data here can measure the public head out-of-embryo, so fixing the test does not produce evidence of a gain.
fix_if_any: No change makes this worth a dedicated LB slot. If the team wants it anyway: (1) do not loosen gate (b). Add a bias-removed error column to train_coordhead.py (sqrt(mean^2 - |bias|^2) per embryo), because uniform offsets are free under the 7 um metric. Require blend <= 0.97 x public on the bias-removed error in BOTH embryo-held-out directions AND on 44b6 leak5. (2) Measure the node-count change of the blend in a full-pipeline lab run with the x138 tail on the 6bba lab cache, and reject it if |dNodes| > 0.5%, so node-multiplier artefacts (+-0.001-0.003) cannot pose as localisation. (3) If it passes, ride it on a submission already planned (for example F1 + blend, W=0.5) rather than a standalone probe, and never pick a final on the blend's LB delta alone: it is below the noise. A cheaper alternative with the same averaging bonus and no convention risk: average the public head with a second public-recipe head (20-40 movies from both embryos, embryo-debiased, x138 hyperparameters). That fixes the 'more movies' question without the 6bba-dominated composite.
realistic_public_gain: +0.001 (range -0.001 to +0.003; P(>= +0.002) ~0.2). It would be scored only if the gate passes (P ~0.1-0.15), so the expected realised gain is ~+0.0002.
realistic_private_gain: +0.0008 (range -0.0015 to +0.0025). The private embryos are unseen by both heads. Single-embryo transfer tests show Q-type heads losing their in-embryo edge (6bba bias-removed 1.336 -> 1.424 out-of-embryo) and trailing the public head on 44b6-like data by +3..+4%.
critical_path: Logistically feasible. 25 Sep evening: agent adds --blend-public to tools/train_coordhead.py (~2 h). The user or friend A runs the ~5 min CPU gate on the Windows PC that holds experiments/coordhead_retrain/captures (they are not in this container). Only if the gate passes (P ~0.1-0.15): 26 Sep ~02:00 kernel (x138 + blend, private head dataset), ~04:00 dummy run on sasyami (0.7 GPU-h), ~05:00 submit, scored ~13:00-16:00 UTC 26 Sep. Most likely outcome: the gate fails on 44b6 (gate b) and no LB slot is used.
